1939-09-01.headline: Germany invades Poland
1939-09-01.summary: At 04:45 the battleship Schleswig-Holstein opens fire on the Polish depot at Westerplatte. German armies cross the frontier from Pomerania, Silesia and East Prussia. Wieluń is bombed at dawn with no military target of note. Danzig declares its annexation to the Reich.

events.name: Westerplatte
events.text: 182 Polish soldiers begin a seven-day defence against naval gunfire and Stuka attack.

events.name: Wieluń
events.text: Struck at 04:40 by Ju 87s. Roughly 70% of the town destroyed; hundreds of civilians killed.

events.name: Mokra
events.text: The Wołyńska Cavalry Brigade holds off the 4th Panzer Division for a day.

1939-09-02.headline: The frontier gives way
1939-09-02.summary: German armour breaks through at Mokra and Częstochowa. In the Corridor, Polish forces are split. The Luftwaffe has effective command of the air over most of the country.

events.name: Częstochowa
events.text: Taken by the 10th Army; reprisal killings follow on 4 September.

1939-09-03.headline: Britain and France declare war
1939-09-03.summary: Chamberlain's ultimatum expires at 11:00; Britain declares war, France follows at 17:00. No offensive in the west materialises. The Battle of the Corridor ends with Pomerelia in German hands.

events.name: London
events.text: "This country is at war with Germany." The declaration brings no immediate relief to Poland.

1939-09-04.headline: Across the Warta
1939-09-04.summary: German forces force the Warta. Polish command orders a general withdrawal to the Vistula–San line, abandoning the western provinces.

1939-09-05.headline: The Battle of the Border ends
1939-09-05.summary: The frontier defences have been broken along their length. Polish armies are in retreat everywhere, harried from the air and unable to break contact.

1939-09-06.headline: Kraków falls; the government leaves Warsaw
1939-09-06.summary: Kraków is abandoned without a fight. The Polish government and high command evacuate Warsaw for Lublin, beginning a retreat that will end at the Romanian border.

events.name: Kraków
events.text: Occupied without resistance; it becomes the seat of the General Government.

1939-09-07.headline: Westerplatte surrenders
1939-09-07.summary: After seven days, Major Sucharski surrenders the depot. The German commander permits him to keep his sabre. Polish forces begin organising the defence of Warsaw.

events.name: Westerplatte
events.text: Holds seven days against an expected twelve hours.

1939-09-08.headline: Panzers reach Warsaw
1939-09-08.summary: The 4th Panzer Division reaches the Ochota suburb and attempts to take the city on the move. The attack is thrown back with heavy loss. The siege of Warsaw begins.

events.name: Warsaw
events.text: The first armoured assault is repelled by improvised barricades and anti-tank guns.

1939-09-09.headline: The Bzura counterattack
1939-09-09.summary: The Poznań and Pomorze Armies strike south across the Bzura into the German 8th Army's exposed flank — the largest battle of the campaign and the only major Polish offensive.

events.name: Bzura
events.text: Around 225,000 Polish troops attack. The offensive stalls German operations for a week.

1939-09-10.headline: Bzura at its high-water mark
1939-09-10.summary: Polish forces retake Łowicz and press south. The German command diverts armour from Warsaw to contain the breakthrough.

1939-09-11.headline: The tide turns on the Bzura
1939-09-11.summary: German reinforcements arrive from three directions. The Luftwaffe is concentrated over the battlefield in the campaign's heaviest air effort.

1939-09-12.headline: Abbeville: no offensive in the west
1939-09-12.summary: The Anglo-French Supreme War Council meets at Abbeville and resolves against a general offensive on the Western Front. Poland will fight alone.

events.name: Abbeville
events.text: The decision is not communicated to the Polish government.

1939-09-13.headline: The pocket closes
1939-09-13.summary: German forces begin to encircle the Bzura armies. Polish units attempt to break through toward Warsaw.

1939-09-14.headline: Warsaw encircled
1939-09-14.summary: The 3rd Army closes the ring east of Warsaw. Gdynia falls after a fortnight's defence; the surviving garrison withdraws to the Hel Peninsula.

events.name: Gdynia
events.text: Falls after two weeks. Defenders fall back onto Hel.

1939-09-15.headline: Białystok taken; Brest invested
1939-09-15.summary: German forces reach Białystok and lay siege to the fortress at Brest-Litovsk.

events.name: Brest
events.text: Defended by a scratch garrison under General Plisowski.

1939-09-16.headline: Brest fortress falls
1939-09-16.summary: The citadel is taken after four days. Polish forces on the Bzura are compressed into a shrinking pocket around Kampinos.

1939-09-17.headline: The Soviet Union invades
1939-09-17.summary: At dawn the Red Army crosses the eastern frontier on the pretext that the Polish state has ceased to exist. Polish forces are ordered not to engage except in self-defence. That night the government crosses into Romania.

events.name: Eastern frontier
events.text: Two Soviet fronts, roughly 600,000 men, advance against a thin border screen.

events.name: Kuty
events.text: The Polish government crosses into Romania and is interned.

1939-09-18.headline: The two armies meet
1939-09-18.summary: German and Soviet forces make contact near Brest. The Polish government is interned in Romania, ending organised state direction of the war.

1939-09-19.headline: The Bzura ends
1939-09-19.summary: The Bzura pocket collapses; some 170,000 Polish soldiers go into captivity. Lwów is now besieged from the west by Germans and from the east by Soviets.

events.name: Lwów
events.text: Besieged from both sides at once — the only city so encircled in the campaign.

1939-09-20.headline: Fighting around Lwów
1939-09-20.summary: Skirmishes between German and Soviet units outside Lwów before the demarcation is settled by negotiation.

1939-09-21.headline: The Germans withdraw from Lwów
1939-09-21.summary: Under the agreed demarcation, German forces pull back west of the San, leaving Lwów to the Red Army.

1939-09-22.headline: Lwów surrenders; joint parade at Brest
1939-09-22.summary: General Langner surrenders Lwów to the Soviets on terms that are not honoured — officers are arrested. At Brest, Guderian and Krivoshein hold a joint parade to mark the handover.

events.name: Brest
events.text: German and Soviet troops parade together as the city changes hands.

events.name: Lwów
events.text: Surrendered to the Red Army. The garrison's officers are deported.

1939-09-23.headline: Krasnobród
1939-09-23.summary: One of the last cavalry-versus-cavalry actions in European warfare is fought at Krasnobród.

events.name: Krasnobród
events.text: A Polish squadron charges and takes the town.

1939-09-24.headline: Warsaw under bombardment
1939-09-24.summary: Artillery and air attack on Warsaw intensify. The city is without reliable water or power.

1939-09-25.headline: Black Monday
1939-09-25.summary: Around 1,150 German sorties strike Warsaw in the heaviest air attack of the campaign, dropping some 560 tons of bombs. Fires burn unchecked; the waterworks are destroyed.

events.name: Warsaw
events.text: "Black Monday." Casualties among civilians run into the thousands.

1939-09-26.headline: The city cannot hold
1939-09-26.summary: With no water to fight fires and no prospect of relief, the Warsaw command opens negotiations.

1939-09-27.headline: Terms agreed
1939-09-27.summary: General Rómmel accepts surrender terms for Warsaw. Underground resistance is organised the same day as Service for Poland's Victory.

1939-09-28.headline: Warsaw capitulates; the partition is signed
1939-09-28.summary: Warsaw surrenders after twenty days; some 140,000 troops go into captivity and roughly 25,000 civilians have been killed. In Moscow, Ribbentrop and Molotov sign the German-Soviet Boundary and Friendship Treaty, fixing the partition along the Bug.

events.name: Warsaw
events.text: Capitulates after a twenty-day siege.

events.name: Moscow
events.text: The Boundary and Friendship Treaty redraws the line, trading central Poland for Lithuania.

1939-09-29.headline: Modlin surrenders
1939-09-29.summary: The fortress at Modlin, out of ammunition and crowded with wounded, surrenders after sixteen days.

events.name: Modlin
events.text: Surrenders with 24,000 men, 4,000 of them wounded.

1939-09-30.headline: A government in exile
1939-09-30.summary: Władysław Sikorski forms a Polish government-in-exile in Paris. The Polish state continues in law and in the field, if not in territory.

events.name: Paris
events.text: Sikorski becomes Prime Minister; Raczkiewicz, President.

1939-10-01.headline: German troops enter Warsaw
1939-10-01.summary: The occupation of the capital begins. On the Baltic, Hel is still fighting.

1939-10-02.headline: Hel surrenders
1939-10-02.summary: The Hel Peninsula, bombarded from land, sea and air for a month, capitulates.

events.name: Hel
events.text: The last coastal position surrenders after 32 days.

1939-10-03.headline: Kleeberg turns to fight
1939-10-03.summary: The Independent Operational Group Polesie, marching to relieve Warsaw and finding it already fallen, turns and engages German forces near Kock.

events.name: Kock
events.text: General Kleeberg's 17,000 men fight the campaign's last battle.

1939-10-04.headline: Kock continues
1939-10-04.summary: Kleeberg's force holds its ground and counterattacks, taking prisoners on the second day of the battle.

1939-10-05.headline: Victory parade in Warsaw
1939-10-05.summary: Hitler reviews German troops on Aleje Ujazdowskie. Eighty kilometres away, the fighting has not stopped.

events.name: Warsaw
events.text: The victory parade is held while the Battle of Kock is still being fought.

1939-10-06.headline: The last surrender
1939-10-06.summary: Out of ammunition, General Kleeberg surrenders at Kock. Organised resistance in Poland ends after thirty-six days. Roughly 200,000 Polish soldiers evade capture or escape abroad to fight on.

events.name: Kock
events.text: The last field formation lays down its arms.
